EventItemActionText:
The Board of Architectural Review met in a regular session on Thursday, December 19, 2024, at 7:30 p.m. in Town Hall, 127 Center St S, Vienna, VA 22180.

Roll Call: Ms. Couchman, Mr. Penati, Mr. O’Keefe, and Ms. Hanley were present. 

Absent member: Mr. Cheselka 

Staff present: Planner Sharmaine Abaied, and Board Clerk Yaska Camacho Castillo.

Request approval of two new building signs and a tenant panel replacement for Dar Mariam located at 107 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1509623-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district; filed by Chang Lee, Samsung Sign and Awning, Project Contact.

Applicant present: Mariam Al-timeemy, Business owner. 

The applicant stated that the landlord specifically requested raceway signage and mentioned that the sign contractor wanted the board members to know that the sign would be painted to match the building's façade. 

Ms. Abaied noted that the sign company submitted updated renderings. The sign facing the façade is 6 inches of space above and below the channel letter sign facing Center Street and 3 inches above and below the sign facing Maple Avenue West. 
Ms. Hanley asked for the meaning of the letters next to the word Maraim to which the applicant stated it means Dar Mariam in Arabic. 

The board voiced their concerns about the blue color not contrasting with the brown background making it difficult for customers to identify the sign. While the color blue is nice, it doesn’t have enough contrast or definition on its own. 

Mr. Penati suggested adding a white outline around the blue to enhance the visibility. Ms. Couchman suggested using light blue if the applicant didn’t want to use white for the outline. The applicant understood the board's concerns and agreed with the suggestion to add a white outline since it would match the white wording in Arabic. 

Ms. Couchman made a motion to approve the request for two new building signs and a tenant panel replacement for Dar Mariam located at 107 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1509623-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district; filed by Chang Lee, Samsung Sign and Awning, Project Contact with the condition that both signs on the building have white returns to match the Arabic letter. 

Motion: Ms. Couchman 
Second: Mr. O’Keefe
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 107 Maple Ave W - Dar Mariam - Signs

EventItemActionText:
Request of a new sign for Trippy Smoke Shop, located at 513 Maple Ave W., Docket No. PF-1476338-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district; filed by Gloria Walker of Signarama, Project Contact.

Applicant Present: No Show when called at 7:43 p.m

Ms. Abaied stated that she notified the applicant that someone needed to be present at the meeting to present the application. 

Ms. Hanley stated that the shopping center has many box signs that are typically replaced without creating entirely new ones, maintaining consistency with the surrounding area over the past 20-30 years. However, there's a new box sign being added beneath an existing one. She is interested in seeing if this new sign can replicate the older ones, or if a different design would be more suitable. She mentioned a past example where the Vienna Art Society used flush-mounted letters on an arch beneath the sign, which looked aesthetically pleasing.

Ms. Abaied noted that the business is in suite 200 which is on the second floor. The reason the applicant is proposing a new sign is that there is no sign box for suite 200. Ms. Hanley responded that there is no way of evaluating without any material specifications. 

Ms. Couhcman mentioned that the signs for Dallas Say Beauty Place and Clyde's Hemp have more space between the windows and top trim, allowing for larger signage. In contrast, the smoke shop can't place its sign in the same way, so its signs are positioned below the windows instead.

The board's concerns are whether the font will be legible, particularly with the inclusion of the word "trippy," and whether the signage will obscure important architectural features like an arch as well as the location of the signage. The board would like for their suggestions stated on record to be relayed to the applicant. 

Mr. O’Keefe made a motion to defer the request for a new sign for Trippy Smoke Shop, located at 513 Maple Ave W., Docket No. PF-1476338-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district; filed by Gloria Walker of Signarama.

Motion: Mr. O’Keefe 
Second: Ms. Couchman
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 513 Maple Ave W - Trippy Smoke Shop - Sign

EventItemActionText:
Request approval for exterior modifications related to the installation of a rooftop structure extending the elevator and sliding glass door, located at 135 Center St. S, Docket No. PF-1553580-BAR, in the RMU, Residential Multi-Unit zoning district, filed by Scott Fleming, Rust Orling Architecture, project contact.

Applicants Present: Scott Fleming, Architecture & Jerry Lahaie, property owner. 

Mr. Fleming discussed the building's design, which features a "dog house" structure with stairs and elevators leading to the terrace. The property owners want the elevator to reach the roof for easy access to supplies. The elevator location is constrained by zoning rules and the existing roof structure, limiting changes. The new design aims to blend in with the existing brick and siding materials, keeping the roof, trim, and windows consistent with the house's design. The roof sheds water from front to back, requiring a new downspout due to the addition of a structure that disrupts the drainage. There's discussion about potentially rerouting the downspout to align with the front tower feature, though it would require re-roofing part of the area. Ms. Hanley asked if the overflow scupper could run along the base of the cornice on the outside of the building over the architectural feature and drop straight down. The discussion continued. 

Mr. O’Keefe suggested keeping the downspouts white instead of painting them red, as painting could create a maintenance issue if the surface is not pre-finished. 

Mr. Penati wondered about the patio door. The applicant confirmed that the new patio door will match the existing windows in color and style, specifically using the same Anderson 200 series line. 

Ms. Hanley expressed concern about the visibility of a maintenance door on the roof side, questioning if it would be visible from the public street. She suggested minimizing the height of the door, possibly using a smaller, code-compliant door, as it will only be for maintenance access. She also noted that using a standard-sized door would be preferable to avoid the high cost of special-order exterior doors.

Mr. Fleming believes the maintenance door won't be visible from the surrounding area because it's tucked away. He suggests painting it to match the siding and reducing it to a solid 6-8 door.

Mr. Penati made a motion to approve the request for exterior modifications related to the installation of a rooftop structure extending the elevator and sliding glass door, located at 135 Center St. S, Docket No. PF-1553580-BAR, in the RMU, Residential Multi-Unit zoning district, filed by Scott Fleming, Rust Orling Architecture, with the condition that a lateral be added to the existing downspout and move the downspout to the (corner) architectural feature.  

Motion: Mr. Penati
Second: Ms. Couchman
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 135 Center St S - Townhome - Exterior Modification

EventItemActionText:
Ms. Hanley was recused from item 4 as she was the applicant representing the application. Vice Chair Mr. O’Keefe stepped in as the chair for this item. 

Item No 4: Request approval of minor revision to the stair risers and columns to building one for Grove on Park (formerly Vienna Courts), located at 127 – 133 Park St NE, Docket No. PF-983578-BAR, in the RMU, Residential - Multi-Unit zoning district, filed by Patty Hanley of BFR Construction Company, project contact.

Applicant Present: Patty Hanley 

Ms. Hanley explained that there was some confusion in the application, leading to incorrect materials being listed for the risers and columns. They decided that stucco would not be suitable for the risers and instead opted for brick, which was their original intention. The columns will also be brick, as shown in their correct images. These changes are now being made official to the board. 

Ms. Couchman made a motion to approve the request for minor revision to the stair risers and columns to building one for Grove on Park (formerly Vienna Courts), located at 127 – 133 Park St NE, Docket No. PF-983578-BAR, in the RMU, Residential - Multi-Unit zoning district, filed by Patty Hanley of BFR Construction Company, project contact, as submitted. 

Motion Ms. Couhcman 
Second Mr. Penati
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 127-133 Park St NE - The Grove on Park - Exterior Modification (Revision)

EventItemActionText: Ms. Couchman was elected as the BAR Secretary for a 3-year term which is when the board will elect all the officers again. Vote 3-0.

The architects from Patrick Henry Library resubmitted their plans, which now include a design that follows the brick all the way across. This was not what the board originally approved, but the applicant is willing to come back for a revision. The modification was presented to the board for review, showing how the revised design would look. The board was pleased with the modification and stated if the applicant wants to move forward with the revision they can submit the application to be officially presented to the board.
The board discussed several aspects of outdoor dining, fences, and furniture choices.
